extra_misconceptions.fact: Sweeping launches fine crystalline silica dust into the air, where it can cause permanent lung damage unless wet-mopped.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dry sweeping studio floors after trimming pots is the fastest and safest way to keep a pottery workspace clean.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Toxic heavy metals in raw glazes can enter the body through skin cuts, airborne dust inhalation, or hand-to-mouth contact.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Lead-bearing and barium-heavy raw glaze chemicals are harmless unless you accidentally swallow the liquid mixture.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Glowing kilns emit intense infrared and ultraviolet radiation that requires shade 3 to shade 5 welding or kiln-viewing glasses.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standard sunglasses provide full eye protection when looking inside a glowing kiln peephole to check pyrometric cones.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Heavy clay and glaze particles settle rapidly inside plumbing traps and harden like concrete without a sediment clay trap.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leftover clay slurry and thick glaze rinse water can be poured directly down a standard household sink drain safely.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to sweep dried clay dust with a dry broom instead of mopping studios with water?
Which rating on a respirator mask is required when mixing dry silica-bearing clay powders or glazes?
What happens to loose sleeves, long hair, or dangling jewelry near a spinning electric potter's wheel?
Under what condition is it safe to open a top-loading electric kiln lid after a high-temperature firing?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Grog is pre-fired ground ceramic that adds structural tooth, reduces drying shrinkage, and prevents warping in thick sculptures.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Coarse grog is added to clay bodies primarily to make the wet clay feel softer and smoother on the potter's hands.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fine porcelain has low wet strength and high shrinkage, causing thick hand-built walls to slump or crack during drying.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Highly plastic, ultra-fine porcelain clay is the easiest clay body for building tall, thick-walled hand-built sculptures.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A kick wheel is spun by kicking a heavy horizontal flywheel, whereas a treadle wheel uses a swinging foot lever and crankshaft.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A treadle wheel and a traditional flywheel kick wheel use the exact same foot-pushing motion to spin the wheel head.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excess water washes away fine plastic platelets and weakens the clay wall, causing the thrown vessel to collapse quickly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding extra water to a short, non-plastic clay body on the wheel permanently restores its lost elasticity and strength.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a large hand-built clay sculpture during drying if the clay body lacks coarse grog?
Why does a wheel-throwing clay body need fine particle size and high plasticity instead of heavy grog?
Which mechanical principle allows a heavy flywheel on a momentum kick wheel to maintain steady rotation?
What physical test with a coiled clay rope confirms whether a clay body has enough plasticity to throw?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pointed amphora bases allowed ships to wedge oil and wine jars upright into sand or wooden racks and helped pour heavy loads.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Greek amphorae were built with pointed bases because ancient potters did not know how to flatten a vessel foot.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Clay shrinks during both air drying and kiln vitrification, so wet forms must be scaled larger than the target finished size.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A ceramic mug thrown to match the exact height of a paper drawing will stay that exact height after firing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Spout tip height must align above the water line so liquid does not spill prematurely when filling the teapot body.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Decorative handles and spouts on a functional teapot design only need to look balanced from the side profile view.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Traditional Pueblo pottery was hand-built using pinched bases and clay coils, then scraped smooth with gourd ribs and polished.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pueblo coil pots from the American Southwest were historically thrown on high-speed electric wheels before painting.

extra_socratic_questions: Which vessel proportions on your historical drawing reveal whether the pot stored grain, water, or olive oil?
What measurement on your original design drawing accounts for the 10 to 15 percent shrinkage of fired clay?
Where should the center of gravity sit on a tall vase drawing so the finished ceramic piece does not tip?
Why is it important to sketch both the exterior silhouette and the interior wall thickness cross-section?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wedging expels trapped air pockets, aligns clay platelets, and homogenizes moisture throughout the lump before forming.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wedging clay on a plaster table is done to whip tiny air bubbles into the clay so it feels lighter when throwing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pyrometric cones measure heat-work, which combines both peak temperature and the duration of heating over time.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A pyrometric cone bends at one exact temperature regardless of how fast or slow the kiln heats up during firing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Handles and trims must be completed at the leather-hard stage because bone-dry greenware is brittle and will crack or pop off.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bone-dry greenware is safe to trim and attach handles to because all physical water has evaporated from the pores.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fired earthenware remains porous and permeable to liquids unless sealed with a melted glass-forming glaze layer.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Earthenware clay vitrifies into a completely non-porous, waterproof ceramic body even without applying a surface glaze.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator tells a potter that a clay pot has transitioned from leather hard to bone dry?
Why does a pyrometric cone measure cumulative heat-work better than a digital thermocouple thermometer alone?
What happens to a bone-dry greenware cup if you place it directly into a bucket of water versus bisque ware?
Under what condition should two clay pieces be scored and slipped together to prevent separation in the kiln?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thick solid clay walls trap moisture deep inside, turning to steam above 212 degrees Fahrenheit and exploding in the kiln.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hollowing out a thick clay animal sculpture is unnecessary as long as you compress the outside surface with a rib.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Melted glaze acts like molten glue at peak temperature and permanently fuses touching pots or un-waxed feet to the kiln shelf.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Glaze-fired pots can touch each other and rest directly on bare kiln shelves just like unfired bisque greenware.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bracing your elbows firmly against your hips or thighs transfers core body stability to the clay and stops wheel wobble.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Centering clay on the wheel requires gripping the clay with finger strength while holding your arms out in the air.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Leaving a quarter-inch to half-inch floor at the bottom before pinching upward prevents a thin, cracking base.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pinch pots should be formed by pressing your thumbs all the way through the bottom of the clay ball first.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to load a thick-walled clay sculpture into a kiln before it reaches the bone-dry state?
What happens to a glazed pot during a high-temperature glaze firing if the foot ring is not wiped clean?
Where should the potter anchor their elbows when centering a wobbling ball of clay on a spinning wheel head?
Which step in joining two leather-hard slabs prevents the seam from cracking open as the vessel shrinks?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Industrial ceramics span aerospace heat shields, fiber optics, semiconductor substrates, catalytic converters, and medical implants.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The United States ceramic industry consists almost entirely of handmade decorative mugs, bowls, and garden flowerpots.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Engineered silicon carbide and boron carbide ceramics combine extreme hardness with low weight to stop projectiles and resist heat.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Ceramic materials are never used in military armor or aircraft engines because all ceramics shatter under any stress.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Vitrified electrical porcelain is a premier dielectric insulator that blocks high-voltage current from arcing to metal towers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Porcelain is used inside high-voltage electrical substations because fired clay is an excellent conductor of electricity.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Medical-grade zirconia and alumina bioceramics are chemically inert, wear-resistant, and biocompatible inside the human body.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Artificial ceramic bone and tooth implants corrode and dissolve rapidly when exposed to human blood and tissue fluids.

extra_socratic_questions: Why are high-voltage power line insulators and automotive spark plugs manufactured from technical porcelain?
Which ceramic material property protects a spacecraft heat shield from melting during atmospheric reentry?
What makes bioceramics like alumina and zirconia suitable for artificial hip joints and dental implants?
Under what industrial operating condition do steel mills line blast furnaces with refractory ceramic bricks?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Electric kilns heat with metallic resistance coils in an oxidation atmosphere, since fuel reduction corrodes heating elements.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Electric kilns routinely operate in heavy reduction atmospheres by burning off the oxygen inside the firing chamber.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Low-fire raku ware remains porous, fragile, and crazed from thermal shock, making it unsuitable for food or microwave use.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Raku pottery pulled red-hot from a kiln and smoked in leaves is dense and safe for holding hot soup or coffee.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Vaporized sodium injected at peak heat reacts directly with silica in the clay surface to form a natural orange-peel glaze.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Salt and soda kilns require every pot to be dipped in thick liquid glaze before loading the firing chamber.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Restricting the damper starves the chamber of oxygen, creating a reduction atmosphere where carbon pulls oxygen from metal oxides.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Closing the chimney damper on a gas kiln increases oxygen flow and makes the kiln fire cleaner and cooler.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to copper-bearing glaze colors in a gas kiln when the damper is closed to create reduction?
Why do potters pull glowing red-hot raku ware out of the kiln with tongs and place it into dry sawdust?
What chemical reaction occurs when rock salt or sodium carbonate is introduced into a white-hot soda kiln?
Which visual clue on a museum ceramic vessel distinguishes an oxidation firing from a wood-ash firing?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ceramics careers include materials science engineering, industrial mold making, museum conservation, teaching, and glaze chemistry.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Selling handmade bowls at weekend craft fairs is the only full-time career path available in the ceramics field.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Ceramic engineers formulate inorganic compounds, test thermal and electrical properties, and scale manufacturing for industry.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A ceramic materials engineer spends their workday throwing clay pots on an electric wheel in an art studio.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Conservators stabilize archaeological ceramics using reversible adhesives and chemical cleaning without refiring original artifacts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Museum ceramic conservators repaint and re-fire broken ancient pottery in a high-temperature kiln to repair cracks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Successful studio potters manage kiln maintenance, raw material batch testing, pricing margins, shipping, and safety compliance.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Production studio potters only need artistic talent and never need to track firing costs, glaze inventory, or kiln logs.

extra_socratic_questions: Which university degree prepares a specialist to design refractory tiles and semiconductor ceramic substrates?
What daily technical tasks differentiate a ceramic materials engineer from an independent studio production potter?
Why do industrial tableware manufacturers employ slip-casting mold makers alongside CAD product designers?
Where can an aspiring studio potter gain hands-on kiln management experience after completing undergraduate classes?
